At 632 pm, NWS Springfield issued Severe Thunderstorm Warning #243 for the Branson
area and the Table Rock Lake areas near Branson. An e-mail notification of SVR #243
was sent to RTDB by its weather monitoring subscription service.

units.qualifier: lead time between the severe thunderstorm warning and the events it preceded
units.mapping: both measure from the 1832 / 632 pm issuance but to different reference events: NTSB to each vessel's water entry (632 pm + 13 min = 645 pm / 1845 for the first duck boat, 632 pm + 23 min = 655 pm / 1855 for the Stretch Duck 7); SA to the arrival of strong winds at the accident point (632 pm + 28 min = 700 pm)

sources.stated_value: all four duck boats entered the water after the warning was issued: the first one, 13 minutes afterward; the Stretch Duck 7, 23 minutes later
sources.quote:
In fact, all four duck boats conducting tours on the evening of the accident entered the water
after the warning was issued: the first one, 13 minutes afterward; the Stretch Duck 7, 23 minutes
later.

sources.stated_value: Severe Thunderstorm Warning #243 was issued at 632 pm, roughly 28 minutes before the arrival of strong winds at the point of the accident
sources.quote:
Importantly, Severe Thunderstorm Warning #243 was issued at 632
pm, roughly 28 minutes before the arrival of strong winds at the point of the accident.

units.qualifier: storm movement and maximum gust carried in the 1832 / 632 pm warning text
units.mapping: both give 50 mph as the movement stated in the warning, the NTSB attributing it to the thunderstorms and the SA to the gust front; the SA adds the measured speed, 58 - 50 = 8 mph faster than the warned value

sources.stated_value: The warning advised of thunderstorms moving at 50 mph with wind gusts of 60 mph
sources.quote:
The warning advised of thunderstorms moving at 50 mph with wind gusts of
60 mph.

sources.stated_value: speed of movement in SVR #243 was noted at 50 mph, which was slightly slower than the 58 mph measured
sources.quote:
For SVR #243 issued at 632 pm, speed of movement in the warning was noted at 50 mph, which
was slightly slower than the 58 mph measured.

units.qualifier: time the Stretch Duck 7 and the other duck boats entered Table Rock Lake
units.mapping: 1855 - 1200 = 655 pm, so the NTSB's Stretch Duck 7 entry time is the SA's 655 pm; the NTSB additionally times the other three vessels at 1845, 1847 and 1854, which the SA does not report

sources.stated_value: the Stretch Duck 27 entered the lake at 1845, the Stretch Duck 17 at 1847, the Stretch Duck 54 at 1854, and the Stretch Duck 7 at 1855
sources.quote:
the Stretch Duck 27 entered the lake at 1845, the Stretch Duck 17 at 1847, the
Stretch Duck 54 at 1854, and the Stretch Duck 7 at 1855.

sources.stated_value: At 655 pm, SD7 entered the water; the water appeared calm at the time
sources.quote: At 655 pm, SD7 entered the water. The water appeared calm at the time. (source NTSB)

units.qualifier: how far the gust front ran ahead of the storm's precipitation
units.mapping: different units and different reference features for the same lead: NTSB 10-15 statute miles ahead of the heavy rainfall; SA 5-10 nautical miles (about 5.8-11.5 statute miles) ahead of the primary convective updrafts, which it also expresses as 10-15 minutes

sources.stated_value: the gust front was approximately 10-15 miles ahead of the storm system's heavy rainfall and impacted the accident location between 1859 and 1902
sources.quote:
Based on the radar imagery reviewed by the NTSB, the outflow boundary impacted the
accident location between 1859 and 1902, at which times this gust front was approximately 10–
15 miles ahead of the storm system’s heavy rainfall.

sources.stated_value: the outflow boundary and the onset of severe winds was 5-10 nm ahead of the primary convective updrafts; high winds likely preceded the heavy rainfall by as much as 10-15 minutes
sources.quote:
In general,
the outflow boundary and the onset of severe winds was 5-10 nm ahead of the primary
convective updrafts. As a result of this the high winds likely preceded the heavy rainfall by as
much as 10-15 minutes.

units.qualifier: National Weather Service calculated significant wave heights on Table Rock Lake

sources.stated_value: based on 45- to 55-knot winds for 30 minutes, wave heights were between 2.69 and 3.71 feet and could have been as high as 4.23 feet
sources.quote:
The National Weather Service estimated that, based on 45- to 55-knot winds for 30 minutes,
wave heights were between 2.69 and 3.71 feet and could have been as high as 4.23 feet. 65 The wave
period would have been between 2.7 and 3.6 seconds.

sources.stated_value: 45-55 knot winds for 30 minutes gives estimated significant wave heights of 2.69 feet to 3.71 feet, and approximately 4.23 feet with the longest fetch and 60-knot winds
sources.quote:
Utilizing a standard fetch, duration and wind
speed calculation over a period of 45-55 knot winds for 30 minutes results in estimated
significant wave heights of 2.69 feet to 3.71 feet. Taking the longest potential fetch of 3.7 miles
and a wind of 60 knots for 30 minutes would result in significant waves of approximately 4.23
feet.

units.qualifier: how close lightning came to the accident site before the severe winds arrived
units.mapping: NTSB places lightning within 20 miles at 1846 and within 10 miles at 1900; for the same pre-onset window the SA reports the closest cloud-to-ground strike at 13.1 miles and the closest in-cloud flash at 10.9 miles, that is, nothing inside 10 miles

sources.stated_value: lightning was first identified as having occurred within 20 miles of the accident site at 1846 and within 10 miles at 1900
sources.quote:
Lightning, including both cloud-to-ground and intracloud, was first

identified as having occurred within 20 miles of the accident site at 1846 and within 10 miles at
1900.

sources.stated_value: the closest cloud-to-ground strike in the 30 minutes before the onset of severe winds was 13.1 miles away and the closest in-cloud flash was 10.9 miles away
sources.quote:
At Table Rock Lake, the closest cloud-to-ground strike in the 30-minutes before the onset of
severe winds was 13.1 miles away and the closest in-cloud flash was 10.9 miles away (see
Appendix 1).

units.qualifier: time the severe thunderstorm watch e-mail reached Ride The Ducks
units.mapping: same first watch e-mail from the company's weather subscription service, logged at 1128 by the NTSB and at 1129 am by the SA; 1129 - 1128 = a 1-minute difference

sources.stated_value: 1128 e-mail alert for the severe thunderstorm watch issued by the Storm Prediction Center at 1120
sources.quote:

Email Alert
Time

Applicable Message(s) Selected

sources.stated_value: At 1129 am, an e-mail notification of the Watch was sent to RTDB from RTDB's weather monitoring subscription service
sources.quote:
At 1129 am, an e-mail notification of the
Watch was sent to RTDB from RTDB’s weather monitoring subscription service. The
Watch was in effect at the time SD7 entered the water. (source NWS, DOJ)

units.qualifier: time the lightning e-mail alert reached Ride The Ducks
units.mapping: same lightning e-mail alert from the company's weather subscription service: NTSB 1849 = 649 pm, SA 646 pm; 649 - 646 = a 3-minute difference

sources.stated_value: e-mail alerts were sent for the severe thunderstorm warning at 1832 and for an observation of lightning (within 20 miles) at 1849
sources.quote:
Email alerts were sent for the severe
thunderstorm warning at 1832, as well as for an observation of lightning (within 20 miles) at 1849
(investigators were unable to determine whether these emails were read by Ride The Ducks
personnel).

sources.stated_value: At 646 pm, an e-mail lightning alert for the area was sent to RTDB from its weather monitoring subscription service
sources.quote:
At 646 pm, an e-mail lightning alert for the area was sent to RTDB from its weather
monitoring subscription service. (Source DOJ).

units.qualifier: time the captain was told to run the water portion of the tour first
units.mapping: NTSB times the instruction from the vessel's DVR video at 1827 = 627 pm; the SA places the same instruction between 628 pm and 629 pm, a 1 to 2 minute difference

sources.stated_value: at 1827 the operations supervisor, the manager-on-duty, stepped onto the vessel and instructed the captain and driver to go to the water first
sources.quote:
Video from the
vessel’s digital video recorder (DVR) revealed that at 1827, the operations supervisor, who was the
manager-on-duty that afternoon, stepped onto the vessel and instructed the captain and driver to “go
to the water first.”

sources.stated_value: From 628 pm to 629 pm, the Captain of SD7 was told to take the water portion of the tour first by an individual that briefly stepped onto the rear of SD7
sources.quote:
From 628 pm to 629 pm, the Captain of SD7 was told to take the water portion of the tour
first by an individual that briefly stepped onto the rear of SD7

units.qualifier: wave height and wind speed the vessel was exposed to at the time of the accident
units.mapping: NTSB gives 3-5 foot waves and winds over 70 mph; the SA gives a significant wave height (the average of the highest one-third of waves) of up to 4 feet and winds likely near 70 mph, so the SA figure is a one-third average bracketed inside the NTSB's 3-5 foot range and its wind estimate sits at, not above, 70 mph

sources.stated_value: the vessel was exposed to 3- to 5-feet waves and winds over 70 mph
sources.quote:
The Stretch Duck 7 was exposed to severe weather for about 8 minutes before sinking. For a
portion of this time, the vessel was exposed to 3- to 5-feet waves and winds over 70 mph.

sources.stated_value: winds at the time of the accident were likely near 70 mph with significant wave heights potentially as high as 4 feet
sources.quote:
Estimated winds at the time of the accident were likely near 70 mph
(source DOJ) with significant wave heights potentially as high as 4 feet (source NWS)

units.qualifier: peak gust measured at Springfield/Branson Airport upstream of the lake

sources.stated_value: The nearby Springfield/Branson Airport recorded a peak wind gust of 74 mph at 623 pm
sources.quote:
The advancing derecho would produce widespread severe and damaging winds well upstream of
Springfield, and then throughout the city before moving south toward the Branson and Table
Rock Lake areas. The nearby Springfield/Branson Airport recorded a peak wind gust of 74 mph
at 623 pm.

units.qualifier: wind and wave limits on the vessel's certificate of inspection

sources.stated_value: the COI barred water operation "when winds exceed thirty-five (35) miles per hour, and/or the wave height exceeds two (2) feet"
sources.quote:
The COI also stipulated
the weather conditions in which the vessel was not allowed to operate on water: “when winds exceed
thirty-five (35) miles per hour, and/or the wave height exceeds two (2) feet.”

units.qualifier: where and when the storm system first developed
units.mapping: NTSB's development 'before noon' in north central and northeast Kansas is the SA's initiation 'around 1100 am' in north central Kansas; the SA's first severe wind event 'just before noon' fits inside the NTSB's window

sources.stated_value: the storm system began to develop before noon in north central and northeast Kansas, approximately 400 miles northwest
sources.quote:
The storm system that impacted Table Rock Lake that evening began to develop before noon
in north central and northeast Kansas, approximately 400 miles northwest.

sources.stated_value: storms initially developed around 1100 am just ahead of the cold front in north central Kansas, with the first severe wind event just before noon
sources.quote:
Storms initially developed around 1100 am just ahead of the cold front in north central Kansas.
Over the next hour the storms began to increase in coverage and the first severe wind event
occurred just before noon.

units.qualifier: severe convective wind threshold stated in mph and in knots
units.mapping: 58 mph = 50 knots (and 75 mph = 65 knots) in both documents; the NTSB states it as the derecho gust criterion, the SA as the Severe Thunderstorm Warning issuance threshold

sources.stated_value: wind gusts of at least 58 mph (about 50 knots) and several well-separated gusts of 75 mph (about 65 knots) or greater
sources.quote:
The swath of the storm
can extend more than 250 miles with wind gusts of at least 58 mph (about 50 knots) and several
well-separated gusts of 75 mph (about 65 knots) or greater along most of its path.

sources.stated_value: the current Severe Thunderstorm Warning wind threshold of 50 knots (58 mph)
sources.quote:
Some individuals with interests on inland waterways and campgrounds noted the current Severe
Thunderstorm Warning wind threshold of 50 knots (58 mph) was too high for necessary actions
to be taken by susceptible watercraft, recreational vehicles, tents, etc.
